SMTO-GWT-0013 — Gateway identity changed

GUID: f0a8f2ad-3d5a-4a57-ac44-456ee71b79bd
Slug: gateway-identity-changed
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • The computer at this Gateway's address now shows a different security identity from the one SMTO saved. SMTO stopped so it doesn't send work to a computer it can't vouch for.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and find the Gateway's row. An Identity changed badge confirms this problem. SMTO marks the Gateway so it won't be used by mistake.
  2. Ask the person who manages that computer, in person or by phone, whether its Gateway was reinstalled, reset or moved to new hardware. A change nobody expected could mean a different computer is answering at that address.
  3. Only if they confirm the change, select Forget trusted identity, then select Check connection. SMTO then saves the Gateway's new identity and can use it again.
  4. If the change wasn't expected, leave the Gateway alone and don't run tasks there. Don't move unfinished work to another computer either. Work that may have started on the old Gateway should be checked there first.

What success looks like

  • The row shows Connected without the Identity changed badge, and new tasks run on it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that computer or the network. Don't turn off security checks or accept the new identity just to make the error go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway's captured identity or enrollment no longer matches an available trusted record (pinned public key, enrollment revision, endpoint or node changed, or the record is disabled or unavailable).

What this means

  • A pinned public key, captured enrollment revision, endpoint or selected target identity no longer agrees with the current record; some paths also reject an unavailable or disabled captured record. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A pinned public key, captured enrollment revision, endpoint or selected target identity no longer agrees with the current record; some paths also reject an unavailable or disabled captured record.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare captured target identity and enrollment with the current enabled record, then verify any intended key or endpoint change independently.

How to fix it

  • Compare the record's pinned tls_identity_spki_sha256, enrollment revision, endpoint and node with the peer now presenting. Verify the new fingerprint with the Gateway's operator through a trusted channel; only for a confirmed change, re-enroll with Forget trusted identity (the Server's DELETE /api/agent/gateways/<gateway_id>/identity route) and run a health check. Never disable TLS pinning or move an uncertain operation to another target.
  • Verify the intended machine through a trusted channel and refresh its selection. Use explicit re-enrollment only for a confirmed identity change; never transfer an existing uncertain operation to another target.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A newly selected, verified target has matching endpoint, enrollment and public identity before receiving work.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically trust a replacement identity or disable certificate verification.
  • Do not automatically accept a changed peer key.
  • Do not disable TLS pinning to make a connection pass.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-GWT-0003 — Gateway node does not match
